questions.text: Is a child or teenager a central character?
questions.definition: A main viewpoint or focal character is under 18 for most of the story.

questions.text: Is a woman or girl a central character?
questions.definition: At least one main viewpoint or focal character is a woman or girl.

questions.text: Is a man or boy a central character?
questions.definition: At least one main viewpoint or focal character is a man or boy.

questions.text: Does the story follow several equally important characters?
questions.definition: No single protagonist dominates; three or more characters carry comparable weight.

questions.text: Is a nonhuman character central to the story?
questions.definition: A main viewpoint or focal character is an animal, creature, robot, alien or other nonhuman.

questions.text: Is a student a central character?
questions.definition: A main character is enrolled at a school or university during most of the story.

questions.text: Is a detective or investigator a central character?
questions.definition: A main character investigates a crime or mystery, professionally or as an amateur.

questions.text: Does a central character have supernatural abilities established in the premise?
questions.definition: A main character has magical or supernatural powers that are known early, not revealed as a twist.

questions.text: Is a school a major setting?
questions.definition: A substantial part of the main story takes place at school.

questions.text: Does much of it take place in a large city?
questions.definition: A substantial part of the story is set in a large city (real or invented).

questions.text: Does much of it take place in a village or rural area?
questions.definition: A substantial part of the story is set in a village, countryside or farmland.

questions.text: Does much of it take place in Korea?
questions.definition: A substantial part of the story is set in Korea.

questions.text: Does much of it take place in Britain?
questions.definition: A substantial part of the story is set in England, Scotland, Wales or Northern Ireland.

questions.text: Does much of it take place in the United States?
questions.definition: A substantial part of the story is set in the United States as it exists or existed.

questions.text: Is it mainly set in an invented world?
questions.definition: Most of the story takes place in a fictional world or land that is not our Earth.

questions.text: Does a major part take place aboard a ship or at sea?
questions.definition: A substantial part of the story is set on a ship or at sea.

questions.text: Is most of the story set before 1900?
questions.definition: Most of the story's events happen before 1900 on our calendar. Not the publication year.

questions.text: Is most of it set between 1900 and 1945?
questions.definition: Most events happen from 1900 to 1945 inclusive. Not the publication year.

questions.text: Is most of it set between 1946 and 1999?
questions.definition: Most events happen from 1946 to 1999 inclusive. Not the publication year.

questions.text: Is most of it set in the 2000s or later, excluding an imagined future?
questions.definition: Most events happen in 2000 or later in a present-day setting, not a speculative future.

questions.text: Is it set in an imagined future?
questions.definition: The story is set in a future relative to when it was written.

questions.text: Does it take place across multiple historical periods?
questions.definition: Substantial parts are set in clearly different historical eras.

questions.text: Has a large disaster already changed society when the story begins?
questions.definition: A war, plague, collapse or catastrophe has already reshaped society before the story opens.

questions.text: Is a real historical war a major part of the setting?
questions.definition: A real war (e.g. the Korean War, WWII) is a major part of the setting or plot.

questions.text: Is solving a crime a main storyline?
questions.definition: Investigating or solving a crime is one of the main storylines.

questions.text: Is a romantic relationship a main storyline?
questions.definition: A romantic relationship is one of the main storylines, not a side plot.

questions.text: Is a long journey a main storyline?
questions.definition: Travelling a long distance is one of the main storylines.

questions.text: Is surviving physical danger a main storyline?
questions.definition: Staying alive against physical threats is one of the main storylines.

questions.text: Is conflict within a family a main storyline?
questions.definition: Tension or conflict between family members is one of the main storylines.

questions.text: Is resisting a government or authority a main storyline?
questions.definition: Characters resisting or rebelling against a government or ruling power is a main storyline.

questions.text: Is a competition or tournament central to the premise?
questions.definition: A contest, game or tournament is central to the premise.

questions.text: Does the story prominently involve magic?
questions.definition: Magic is openly real and prominent in the story.

questions.text: Is time travel part of the premise?
questions.definition: Characters travel through time as part of the premise.

questions.text: Is space travel part of the premise?
questions.definition: Travel between planets, stars or through outer space is part of the premise.

questions.text: Are ghosts or spirits openly part of the premise?
questions.definition: Ghosts or spirits are openly real in the story, not merely suspected.

questions.text: Are animals that speak or behave like people prominent?
questions.definition: Animals that talk or act like people play a prominent role.

questions.text: Is a prison or confinement a major setting?
questions.definition: A prison, hospital ward, camp or other place of confinement is a major setting.

questions.text: Is a shop or workplace a major setting?
questions.definition: A shop, office or other workplace is a major setting.

questions.text: Is illness a major part of the premise?
questions.definition: Physical or mental illness of a main character is a major part of the premise.

questions.text: Does the story prominently involve moving to another country?
questions.definition: Emigration or relocating to another country is prominent.

questions.text: Is the story intended to be frightening?
questions.definition: Horror, dread or fear is a primary intended effect.

questions.text: Is humor a major part of it?
questions.definition: Comedy, wit or satire is a major part of the reading experience.

questions.text: Does it strongly focus on growing up?
questions.definition: Coming of age is a central theme.

questions.text: Does it strongly focus on social class or inequality?
questions.definition: Social class, wealth gaps or inequality is a central theme.

questions.text: Does it strongly focus on friendship?
questions.definition: Friendship is a central theme.

questions.text: Does it strongly focus on loneliness or isolation?
questions.definition: Loneliness or isolation is a central theme.

questions.text: Does it strongly focus on grief or loss?
questions.definition: Grief or loss is a central theme.

questions.text: Does it strongly focus on moral or philosophical questions?
questions.definition: Moral or philosophical questions are a central theme.

questions.text: Is much of it narrated using “I”?
questions.definition: A substantial part is first-person narration.

questions.text: Does it switch between different characters’ viewpoints?
questions.definition: Narration switches between the viewpoints of two or more characters.

questions.text: Is much of it presented as letters or diary entries?
questions.definition: A substantial part of the text is letters, diary entries or documents.

questions.text: Does it frequently move between past and present?
questions.definition: The narrative repeatedly alternates between different time frames.

questions.text: Is it part of a named series?
questions.definition: The book belongs to a named series or recurring-character sequence.

questions.text: Is it the first book in that series?
questions.definition: The book is the first published volume of its series. Answer No if it is not part of a series.

questions.text: Does it follow a family across more than one generation?
questions.definition: The story follows two or more generations of one family.
